analysis.title: Intuit Inc. AI Headwinds Compound, FY27 Revenue Guidance Lowered
key_insights: Intuit reported F1Q27 upside: revenue $4,354M vs consensus $4,307M (+12.1% YoY vs consensus 11%), non-GAAP operating margin incl. SBC 24.0% vs consensus 21.1%, non-GAAP EPS incl. SBC $2.91 vs consensus $2.47.
Shares fell about 9% after the close on lower Credit Karma guidance and a soft F2Q guide.

Intuit agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68B ($3.31B cash, $368M BSP stock), with close expected in early CY27. All cash proceeds go to incremental FY27 buybacks. RBC views the exit favorably as it removes a drag on growth and management distraction.
Credit Karma revenue grew 9% YoY, below expectations. Higher interest rates reduced demand and consumers shifted to AI-powered discovery faster than expected, which weighed on engagement.

Management said SEO has historically driven less than 1% of Credit Karma traffic and plans to apply the same GEO playbook used in TurboTax and QuickBooks. The AI impact was described as limited to Credit Karma, and the 4-8% three-year Consumer CAGR target was reiterated.
F2Q27 revenue guidance is +6-7% YoY with non-GAAP EPS of $3.17-$3.22, below consensus of $5,109M revenue and $3.73 EPS.
FY27 revenue guidance was lowered to +8-9% YoY from +9-10%, driven entirely by Credit Karma, now +3-7% from +11-13%. Consumer guidance falls to +2-4% from +4-6%.
FY27 GBS revenue (+13-14%), non-GAAP operating income ($8,063-$8,145M) and non-GAAP EPS ($22.88-$23.12) guidance was reiterated, with lower SBC offsetting Credit Karma.
RBC cut its price target to $330 from $385 and kept Outperform. The target applies 10.7x EV/FCF to CY27 FCF. Shares trade at about 9x EV/CY27E FCF.
RBC's target multiple sits below large-cap software because of recent TurboTax underperformance, AI disintermediation debates and uncertainty around the pivot toward new customer acquisition.
RBC cut its FY27 revenue estimate to $23,254M from $23,503M and its FY28 estimate to $24,983M from $25,927M. FY27 EPS rises to $23.01 from $22.78 and FY28 EPS falls to $25.63 from $26.43.
RBC's FY28 FCF estimate falls to $9,028M from $10,348M, and FY27 FCF rises slightly to $8,545M from $8,566M.
F1Q27 free cash flow was $987M vs RBC's $731M and consensus of $549M.
Scenario analysis: upside case $600 (about 18x CY27 EV/FCF), downside case $150 (about 5x), against a current price of $279.52.

RBC says RBC's rating thesis rests on the subscription model (80%+ recurring revenue), leadership in tax and accounting software, GenAI opportunity (with a caution that monetization may take longer than investors expect) and margin expansion toward 40%+ non-GAAP operating margin.
RBC recommends management run a strategic review of Credit Karma and consider a sale, since it is macro-sensitive and not well integrated with core products.

market_movers.rationale: RBC cut its target to $330 from $385 after F1Q27 results and lower Credit Karma guidance, and kept Outperform because it sees Intuit as a net AI beneficiary over time.

sector_views.rationale: RBC applies a below-large-cap-software multiple to Intuit given TurboTax underperformance and AI disintermediation debates. The report gives no explicit sector stance.

earnings_insights: F1Q27 reported (11/19): revenue $4,354M vs consensus $4,307M and RBC's $4,305M; non-GAAP EPS incl. SBC $2.91 vs consensus $2.47 and RBC's $2.46.
F1Q27 reported non-GAAP operating margin incl. SBC 24.0% vs consensus 21.1%; gross margin 78.9% vs consensus 80.5%.
F1Q27 reported free cash flow $987M vs consensus $549M and RBC's $731M.
F2Q27 company guidance: revenue growth +6-7% YoY, non-GAAP EPS $3.17-$3.22. RBC's new F2Q estimates are revenue $4,942M and EPS $3.19, vs prior $5,098M and $4.05 and consensus $5,109M and $3.73.

FY27 company guidance: revenue +8-9% YoY (from +9-10%), non-GAAP operating income $8,063-$8,145M, non-GAAP EPS $22.88-$23.12. RBC's FY27 estimates are revenue $23,254M and EPS $23.01 vs consensus $23,405M and $22.90.
Credit Karma FY27 revenue growth guidance is +3-7% (from +11-13%). Credit Karma F1Q27 revenue grew 9% YoY.
Mailchimp sale to Bending Spoons for about $3.68B, with all cash proceeds earmarked for incremental FY27 buybacks.
risk_factors: Macro sensitivity of small business and consumer growth.
Execution risk from recent acquisitions, most notably Credit Karma and Mailchimp.
Legislation risk if US tax codes become simpler.
Intuit's GenAI strategy may not pan out as expected.
Competition from large software vendors (Oracle NetSuite, Sage Software) and smaller upstarts (Freshworks, Gusto).
Higher interest rates and AI-driven discovery shifts are cutting Credit Karma demand and engagement.

tension_points.bull_case: RBC believes Intuit can be a net beneficiary of AI over time, citing tax and SMB accounting being services-heavy, and says management reported the AI impact as limited to Credit Karma with the 4-8% three-year Consumer CAGR target reiterated.
tension_points.bear_case: Consumers shifted to AI-powered discovery faster than expected, hurting Credit Karma engagement, and the FY27 Credit Karma guide fell to +3-7% from +11-13%. RBC notes AI disintermediation debates justify a below-peer multiple.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further cuts to Credit Karma or Consumer guidance, or AI-driven traffic shifts spreading beyond Credit Karma into TurboTax and QuickBooks.

theme_stances.key_argument: RBC believes the AI opportunity set outweighs the risks longer term despite near-term Credit Karma headwinds.
theme_stances.evidence: we continue to believe the AI opportunity set outweighs the risks
